items.headline: The Premier League is BACK tonight — Arsenal open the title defense vs Coventry
items.body: The long summer's over: reigning champions Arsenal kick off the 2026-27 season at home tonight against newly promoted Coventry City (3pm ET, USA Network). Ten months of football starts here, and the rest of the weekend is stacked — Man United at Hull, Spurs at Brentford, the whole circus rolling back into gear.
items.say: Premier League's back tonight — Arsenal start their title defense against Coventry. Feels like the summer flew by. You got a team you follow?

links.text: NBC Sports · how to watch the new season

items.headline: Russell nicks a shock Sprint pole at Zandvoort — and the title leader ends up in the gravel
items.body: F1's back from the break and it started with a jolt: George Russell pulled a stunner out of nowhere to grab Sprint pole by 0.041s over Lando Norris — after topping neither of the first two segments. Meanwhile 19-year-old points leader Kimi Antonelli slid into the gravel and could only manage fifth. The Sprint runs Saturday, the last-ever Dutch GP on Sunday.
items.say: F1 came back from break and George Russell grabbed a surprise sprint pole while the teenage kid leading the title spun off into the gravel. Should be a fun one at Zandvoort. You keeping up with this season?

items.headline: CS2's $2M finale is in Paris — the Esports World Cup hits the quarterfinals today
items.body: The biggest Counter-Strike event of late summer is down to the business end: the Esports World Cup playoffs are in Paris with $2 million on the line, and today's quarterfinals include a monster Vitality vs Team Spirit clash. Reigning champs The MongolZ are trying to defend, with the grand final at the Accor Arena on Sunday. All free to stream.
items.say: The big Counter-Strike tournament in Paris is down to the quarterfinals today — two million bucks on the line, Vitality vs Spirit is the one to watch. You still follow CS at all?

items.headline: Leadoff bomb, walk-off bomb — Pete Crow-Armstrong bookends a game with home runs
items.body: Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong did something only five players had ever done: he homered on the very first swing of the game, then ended it with a two-run walk-off shot in the 10th to beat the White Sox 7-5. He's the only player besides Vic Power in 1957 to do it starting with a first-pitch leadoff homer. Manager Craig Counsell called it his best game in the bigs.
items.say: A Cubs guy homered on the first pitch of the game AND hit the walk-off to win it — only the sixth player ever to do that. What a way to bookend a night. You catch much baseball?

items.headline: Where it all began — 'The Fast and the Furious' roars back for its 25th anniversary
items.body: Before the space cars and the impossible stunts, it was just a cop, a street racer, and a pile of tuna sandwiches. The original 2001 film is back on the big screen for its 25th anniversary — Vin Diesel, the late Paul Walker, and the quarter-mile that launched a $7 billion franchise. Pure nostalgia fuel.
items.say: They put the original Fast and the Furious back in theaters for its 25th anniversary — the first one, before it got completely ridiculous. Kind of wild it's been that long. You a fan of those movies?

items.headline: Sam Smith's 'Hazel Eyes' is here — a love letter to New York
items.body: Sam Smith's fifth album lands today, and it's their warmest, most personal yet — billed as an ode to New York, where the London native now lives, with help from Feist and Rob Moose. The lead single 'My Guy' is stripped-back and soulful, all that big voice and not much else. Easy Friday listening.
items.say: New Sam Smith album out today — it's supposed to be this whole love letter to New York. The single 'My Guy' is really pretty. What's been on your playlist lately?

items.headline: The greatest dynasty in college hoops gets its documentary — UConn's story drops today
items.body: 'The Dynasty: UConn Huskies' hits Apple TV today — a three-part deep-dive into Geno Auriemma's 40-year juggernaut, the most dominant program in college basketball history. It pulls in basically everyone: Sue Bird, Diana Taurasi, Maya Moore, Breanna Stewart, and current stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd. A must for any hoops fan.
items.say: There's a new doc on Apple TV about the UConn women's basketball dynasty — Sue Bird, Taurasi, all of them. That program has been unbelievable for like 40 years. You watch much college hoops?

items.headline: Jorja Smith goes to the dancefloor — 'What Are The Odds' lands today
items.body: The British soul star's third album is out today, and it's her most danceable yet — reuniting with producer P2J and led by the sultry single 'Alive' featuring Afrobeats superstar Wizkid, its video shot across one sweaty summer night in Paris. Smooth, late-summer stuff.
items.say: New Jorja Smith album out today — she went more dance-y this time, and there's a great one with Wizkid on it. Really good end-of-summer vibe. You know her?

items.headline: Kelsey Mitchell just won't stop scoring — a WNBA record 21 straight 20-point games
items.body: Indiana's Kelsey Mitchell poured in a game-high 37 (a perfect 15-for-15 at the line) and set a WNBA record with her 21st consecutive 20-point game, passing A'ja Wilson. The Fever fell 91-85 to Dallas — Arike Ogunbowale answered with 32 — but Mitchell's run is one of the great hot streaks the league's ever seen.
items.say: Caitlin Clark's teammate Kelsey Mitchell just set a WNBA record — 21 straight games scoring 20-plus, and she went 15-for-15 from the line. The Fever have been fun to watch this year. You catch any WNBA?
